why: rAF throttles when occluded; headful numbers were noisy (rsl redraw 130.7 vs headless 22.5)
evidence: headful vs headless on same artifact

decision: Localize vis-network to /data/ in variants
why: remove CDN latency + enable offline runs; CDN failure proven

decision: Warm-up throwaway run before measuring
why: first 2 launches ~18% cold (baseline min 27 vs 22)

decision: Primary metric = redraw_min; med/p95 secondary
why: min is stable across reps; med/p95 carry scheduler jitter

decision: DPR is not a lever
why: 4x pixels gave +2% redraw -> geometry-bound

decision: Arrow TYPE is not a lever
why: vee/bar/circle all ~ baseline (21-23)

decision: Arrows-on-hover is a lever, capability preserved
why: -64% redraw; direction still shown on hover

decision: Kill in-browser stabilization; bake positions instead
why: -88% load; baking preserves layout quality

decision: Reject smooth:'dynamic'
why: load exploded to 9.6s

decision: Keep dashes/hover/labels/improvedLayout as-is
why: ~0 redraw impact at dpr1

decision: arrows-on-hover stays the top per-frame lever at scale
why: arrow cost grows with edge count
evidence: continuum 9k: v13 x0.33 vs rsl 1.9k x0.36

decision: Do NOT ship physics-off alone; bake positions
why: nosim cuts load -86% but worsens interaction fps (spiral spread)

decision: Use harness/build_base.py for bases, node_limit forced high
why: prior bases were ad-hoc; continuum was the aggregate (283) mislabelled

decision: bake positions is a LOAD lever, not fps/redraw
why: ratio ~1.0 redraw; identical viewport; clean rsl load -74%

decision: Ship bake only paired with arrows-on-hover
why: physics-off path showed worse interaction fps + longtasks in some sessions
evidence: L2t rsl v19 hover 30 vs baseline 135

decision: Drive battery camera by elapsed time (lane L2t)
why: frame-count driver made path variant-dependent -> fps incomparable
evidence: baseline pan 6.0 vs v13 10.4 only after fix

decision: Huge graphs use the community aggregate (2290/8045) as default view
why: full 104k cannot render in canvas-2D; aggregate opens in 2.8s

decision: Ship v21-hover-straight (straight + arrows-on-hover) for dense graphs
why: best capability-preserving redraw on dense edges; keeps dashes

decision: Aggregate still needs edge-culling; levers are not enough
why: pan stuck ~3fps at 8045 edges with any shippable combo

decision: No leftover harness processes; 16 chrome are the user's own
why: checked CIM cmdlines before any kill

decision: Defer arrowheads only above 1500 edges (density-gated)
why: below threshold the render is byte-identical; avoids changing small-graph look
evidence: tests assert both sides of the gate

decision: Cache stabilized layout in localStorage, not build-time bake
why: no vendored position blob; zero Python layout cost; re-open -99%

decision: Offline = CDN with sibling vis-network.min.js onerror fallback
why: don't vendor 686KB into every graph.html; keeps CDN default

decision: Move to sigma.js + graphology (WebGL) for the graph view
why: canvas-2D vis cannot cross the felt-smoothness threshold; sigma pans at 90-110fps vs 4.8-9.2
evidence: lane L7 rsl head-to-head, real GPU

decision: Use interleaved A/B rounds for all gesture measurements
why: The headless host's throughput drifts ~3x between batches (same file 45.8 then 15.2fps), so sequential before/after produces false findings (it did: a phantom '3x regression')
evidence: profile_drag vs ab_drag on the same variant, two batches

decision: Keep vis-network; abandon the sigma/WebGL spike
why: user judged the sigma prototype ugly and it needs a full rewrite (no arrowheads, legend, search, hyperedges, aggregate path)
evidence: user feedback + lane L7 parity gap list

decision: Leaning the node draw during gestures (borderWidth 1.5->0) is the single biggest smoothness lever found
why: ~1900 per-frame ctx.stroke() border calls saturate the raster pipeline; removing them for the gesture length took node drag 15.1->61.6fps and stalls 119/120->4/120
evidence: lane L8 interleaved A/B, 3 rounds, rsl

decision: Gate the lean draw at 800 nodes and hideEdgesOnZoom with it, so small graphs are byte-identical
why: avoids changing the interaction for graphs that were already smooth and keeps the below-threshold promise

decision: Restore borders on a 180ms zoom timer rather than a zoom-end event
why: vis emits no zoom start/end, only per-step 'zoom'

decision: Apply the gesture lean by writing borderWidth onto node instances, not network.setOptions
why: setOptions re-applies the global option but also costs a full synchronous redraw (~80ms rsl, ~200ms aggregate, 670-2000ms at 9142) = one hitch at dragStart and dragEnd; rsl worst frame 188-222ms -> 62-76ms, and per-node originals are needed anyway to restore 3px learning rings

decision: Force one redraw when restoring the lean, not when applying it
why: drag/zoom redraw themselves so applying needs no redraw; vis emits no redraw on pointer-up (measured 0 canvas strokes in 20 frames after release) so the restore would leave borders off until the next interaction

decision: Rebuild the before/after comparison pair from the current revision in the same tick
why: An artifact from an earlier tick is not a safe "before": base-rsl.html differed from a fresh HEAD build on 2150/3876 edges (all direction reversals), so the user was comparing arrows that current main does not produce; two fresh builds are deterministic and both match our build

decision: Never hide edges during a gesture: hideEdgesOnZoom (added by us) and hideEdgesOnDrag (shipped default, inherited) are both removed
why: The user reported lines vanishing while zooming and while panning - the graph appeared to fall apart in motion. Measured before removal: during a pan the shipped build strokes 24240x @ lineWidth 18.13 and ZERO edges; during a zoom it strokes 7752 edge segments per frame (so the shipped build already hid edges on pan; we had added the zoom case)
evidence: probe_borderdraw.mjs pan/zoom stroke+lineWidth histograms on base-rsl-head / base-ours-v4 / base-ours-v5

decision: Make edges cheap instead of absent: batch the edge pass into one ctx.stroke() per (colour, dashes, width) group for the length of the gesture
why: With edges visible the border lean alone only reached x1.41-1.45 and stayed at 89-91/90 stalled frames; 3876 per-edge stroke() calls (~30ms) are the frame. Grouped batching costs 20 strokes for the same 3876 lines, x2.27-5.79 over the shipped build, stalls 8-16/90, with every line/colour/dash still drawn
evidence: probe_edgebatch.mjs (20 strokes, 3876 lineTo, colour set identical to rest) + ab_drag.mjs 3 rounds certified on base-ours-v6

decision: Do NOT lean edges by writing edge.options.smooth / edge.options.width
why: Dead end, proven: vis resolves the draw from the live instance options (Edge.draw -> getFormattingValues -> edgeType.drawLine) and picks the curve implementation class once in updateEdgeType(); mid-gesture all 3876 edges reported smooth:false + width:1 while the canvas still emitted 0 lineTo, and the drawn lineWidth stayed 3.63 because getFormattingValues floors width at max(w, 0.3/scale)
evidence: edge options mutation probe (debug_edgelean.mjs) + vis-network.min.js draw path

decision: Re-derive the batched lineWidth per frame as max(options.width, 0.3/scale) instead of baking it in at gesture start
why: the 0.3/scale floor moves with the zoom, so a width captured at dragStart is wrong by the time the user zooms; the group key carries the unfloored base width and the floor is recomputed each frame

decision: The edge batch falls back to vis's own draw if it throws, and uninstalls itself after 2 errors
why: a throwing drawLine replacement would blank the canvas for that frame; the catch calls the original drawLine and repeated failure disables the lever rather than leaving a broken render

decision: Odd round counts for A/B, and never read a median-of-two
why: The host swings ~3x inside one render mode: the SAME shipped file measured 15.0fps in round 1 and 43.7fps in round 2 of one mode=new run, and median-of-two silently reported the better one (43.7) next to the worse one's jank (89). This is also the most likely reason the user 'felt nothing' - on a host sitting in the fast regime the shipped build is already ~44fps, so the same build that is 15fps here is not 15fps there

decision: The batched edge pass draws the curve vis draws at rest (quadratic through vis's own via point), not a straight line
why: Straight lines are cheaper but they are a visibly different graph in motion: a mid-gesture frame diffed against the resting frame at the same camera changed 82-104% of painted pixels with straight lines versus 1.1-1.8% with the curve. The curve costs nothing measurable (same interleaved run: straight 79.4/69.3/78.5 vs curved 82.9/78.9/80.4 fps node/pan/zoom)
evidence: probe_motion_pixels.mjs on the noborder builds (straight vs curved), results/ab-rsl-v7-certified.csv

decision: Measure gesture fidelity as a pixel diff between the in-motion frame and the resting frame at the same camera, on builds where the other levers are made no-ops
why: Did the graph change while moving? is exactly the class of complaint that started this work (edges vanishing), and it cannot be judged by eye on a dense coloured graph - two screenshots of 3876 edges look 'the same' whether or not every edge moved. Snapshot while the gesture is held, release so vis redraws the frozen camera through its normal path, diff the framebuffers

decision: When taking over vis's draw, reproduce vis's own primitive and verify the arithmetic against vis's own function, rather than eyeballing an approximation
why: _curveTo re-implements BezierEdgeDynamic._getViaCoordinates for continuous smooth edges, and probe_edgebatch.mjs asserts our via against edgeType.getViaNode() for every edge (worst disagreement 0.0 across 3876). Only the grouping differs from vis, which is why the residual diff is dash phase and node endpoints, not edge shape

decision: Every perf measurement must hold harness/bench_lock.py
why: This host drifts ~3x between batches, so two agents measuring concurrently do not just slow each other down - they silently corrupt each other's numbers; the lock makes the serialization explicit, and bench-runs.log becomes the audit trail of every measurement in the lab
evidence: bench_lock.py verified: second agent blocks while the first holds it; stale lock stolen after 20 min; results/bench-runs.log rows

decision: Subagents explore and measure in lane-prefixed scratch variants and report patch text; the loop owner is the single writer of graphify/exporters/html.py
why: Three parallel lanes all want to change the same exporter block, so concurrent edits would conflict and make every measurement unattributable; lane-prefixed filenames (variants/L9-*, results/ab-L9-*) keep the artifacts apart and one writer keeps the shipped artifact coherent

decision: Exporter consumes pre-baked x/y when present (L10): physics off + no stabilization + fit on first open, spiral seed + solver otherwise
why: First open still runs the solver (~2.4s rsl); the localStorage cache only helps re-opens. Shipping stabilized positions removes that cost for shared graphs, and the change is purely additive (no x/y -> byte-identical to before), so it cannot regress an existing export
evidence: L2 load numbers (-74% rsl, -73% gsoc agg) + _l10test.py/_l10test2.py verification + lanes/L10-first-open.md

decision: Close L9 (node-draw batching) with no shipped lever
why: Shadow already off in values (t.shadow === false for all 1886 nodes), DPR already disproven in Phase 2, and fill grouping (208 distinct (colour,radius) pairs) has no safe seam in vis's shape.draw, which interleaves path + fill + shadow + stroke + bbox + label; reimplementing it would break hover/selection/labels/hit-testing for call-overhead savings on a geometry-bound path. Proposed follow-up L12 instead (keep the edge batch on at rest)

decision: Adopt the L11 viewer-experience block (click-to-focus, search fly-to + pulse, fps/frame-time HUD, hide-leaves, legend isolate) as a single UX block
why: The gesture lever is largely done (82fps on rsl) and the remaining gap between fast and a graph someone would love to use is interaction - locating a node among 1886, understanding its neighbourhood, seeing whether the view is actually smooth, taming the 141-community legend. All four are capability-preserving (fade/isolate on demand, restore on background click; nothing deleted) and the gesture A/B shows no regression (node x1.01, pan x0.99, zoom x1.07; jank 17/21/31 -> 17/22/20)
result: adopted (prototype; exporter fold-in is the follow-up)

decision: Focus is hover-only and paints node instance colours; click-to-focus is removed
why: The L11 click-to-focus dimmed 1858/1886 nodes with opacity 0.12 and only restored on a background click, which is the 'colours go dim' report. Hover always ends (blur), so the state cannot get stuck; and options.color.background is the only write that reaches the draw (options.opacity is ignored), while nodesDS.update of 1886 nodes costs 149.6ms
evidence: results/L13-probe.csv + probe_colorwrite.mjs + probe_zoom_health (dim 1884 -> 0 after blur) + lanes/L13-interaction-feel.md

decision: Selection and hover keep the community colour and accent with a white border ring, never a white fill
why: The shipped highlight repainted the node background #ffffff, so selecting or hovering a cluster made it look washed out - the second half of the user's colour complaint. Keeping the fill also keeps the status ring on learning nodes legible

decision: Wheel zoom is eased and cursor-anchored on rAF, with vis's own wheel handler bypassed, clamped to fit/6..min(2.0,fit*12)
why: vis zooms once per wheel event and each event is a full redraw, so a trackpad queues dozens of redraws per frame - the 'zoom freezes the graph' report. One redraw per frame removes the queue; holding the world point under the cursor keeps it aimed. moveTo(animation:false) emits no zoom/pan in 9.1.6, so the lean is driven explicitly. The clamp keeps labels from being blown up (scale 2.0 ceiling)
evidence: results/L13-zoomhealth-v8.txt (p50 16.9 / p95 29.1 / 3 stalls per 98 frames) + measure.mjs same-session v7 18.4fps/2369ms -> v8 46fps/169ms

decision: Keep stabilization at 200 iterations; do not ship a lower iteration cap
why: it30 loads 5x faster (x0.19) but renders a dense hairball with no community structure, which fails the 'a graph I would love to use' bar; it60 (x0.51) is still a visible layout change. The honest first-open win is baking positions (x0.13) which keeps the 200-iteration layout

decision: The stabilization handler is emitted on one line, and a regression test asserts no escape sequence reaches the page
why: 716c421e shipped the handler as a Python string containing a literal backslash-n, so every build since emits '... => {\\n' and the entire main script fails to parse - the page renders no graph at all. A one-line handler removes the escaping question
evidence: test_stabilization_handler_is_valid_js + smoke_view.mjs on the rebuilt v8 artifact

decision: The rest edge batch skips an edge when the edge or either endpoint node is hidden
why: vis only draws an edge whose both endpoints are visible (Body._updateVisibleIndices); getFormattingValues().hidden does not reflect a hidden endpoint, so the cached batch kept painting the 364 edges of a legend-hidden community (the toggle changed 931 px with the batch on vs 9 191 px with it off). Matching vis removes the orphan edges
evidence: probe_capabilities.mjs on v9: hide community 0 -> batch vs vis 13 766 px, only-batch 933 / only-plain 940 (order, not coverage); before the fix 9 191 px vs 931 px on the toggle

decision: Keep the edge batch installed at rest on dense graphs (L12), accepting that it changes which translucent edge is on top at a crossing
why: Rest p50 85.0 -> 79.9 ms (x0.94) and hover 88.0 -> 73.8 (x0.84), all six interleaved pairs favour it, and 3 483 of 3 876 edges stop being individual strokes. It fails the 2%-of-painted bar: 10.22% of painted pixels differ, colour only, coverage equal to +-4 px of 143k, because colour grouping changes stroke order at crossings (nodash control, same order both sides: 1.61%). Crops are indistinguishable to the eye and _REST_EDGE_BATCH = false restores vis at rest

decision: Dashed (confidence) edges are drawn by vis, not by the batch
why: 393 of 3 876 edges on rsl, and the value of the batch is the long solid tail; handing them back costs ~0.4 ms and keeps the confidence texture exactly as vis draws it. They are flagged __leanDash during the group build so the per-frame draw path stays a single boolean check
evidence: probe_capabilities.mjs settled parity; lane L12 results table

decision: The node disc is drawn with one fill instead of a fill plus a border stroke; the size grows by exactly the width the border would have added
why: vis draws a node as a fill of radius size/2 plus a border stroke of world width min(nodeWidth, 1.5/scale) - at the fit scale that stroke is as wide as the node itself, so 1886 hairline strokes per frame cost ~57 ms of an 86 ms resting frame. The exporter paints every node border in the fill colour, so the same disc can be one fill. Hovered and selected nodes keep a real border, because theirs is white and visible
evidence: results/ab-rest-L22-shipped.csv (rest 93.5 -> 22.6 ms x0.24, hover 85.6 -> 21.5 x0.25, 3 rounds interleaved) + cross-build pixel diff 3.02% of painted (AA edge of a 1 px dot) + probe_node_ring.mjs 446 white px after a real click (v10: 446)

decision: The lean gesture lever is removed; the node border is gone for good
why: With the border replaced by a larger fill there is nothing left to drop for the length of a gesture. The removal also ends a visible artefact: while a drag was live the nodes lost their border and therefore half their radius at the fit scale, then grew back on release
evidence: tests/test_html_perf_levers.py (the lean assertions now describe the new scheme) + probe_frame_parts.mjs on the shipped build

decision: The frame HUD rAF loop runs only while the HUD is visible
why: The loop ran for the life of the page, so an idle page woke up 144 times a second to draw nothing. Nothing moved, so this is not a frame-rate win, but it is the difference between a viewer that is running and a viewer that is idle
evidence: probe_idle.mjs: 432 rAF wake-ups in 3 s of silence before, 0 after, 0 draws either way

decision: Fewer solver iterations are rejected: the first open can only get much faster by moving the layout offline
why: 60 iterations open in 2.3 s (x0.22) but the layout collapses - edge crossings 77 173 -> 394 409, community separation 7.23 -> 1.89, and intra-community edges are no longer shorter than inter-community ones. A community-aware seed does not rescue it (181 671 crossings at 60 iterations). improvedLayout is not the cost (x0.99); avoidOverlap 0 buys 17% and changes the picture. The only route to a fast open is the existing --bake path (1 722 ms, x0.16), which still needs the packaging decision
evidence: results/ab-load-L17.csv + results/ab-load-L19.csv + probe_layout.mjs metrics (crossings, separation, intra/inter)

decision: The lean shrinks the node disc for the length of a gesture instead of dropping a border stroke
why: The first version of L22 removed the lean, reasoning that with the border gone there was nothing left to drop. A same-session A/B said otherwise: node drag 37.7 -> 25.3 fps (x0.67), jank 17 -> 67. The lean is about the SIZE of the disc, not the border - a drag draws the small discs and the small discs are cheaper. With the lean restored (v12) the gestures are x1.24 (drag) and x1.35 (pan) against the build it replaces, and the resting frame keeps x0.33

decision: The before/after comparison is against the user own checkout, not against the released main and not against the lab old snapshot
why: There is no single current graphify: the released main (91f4d120) renders the viewer from graphify/export.py and still sets hideEdgesOnDrag: true, the perf branch pre-perf snapshot is two milestones behind, and the user checkout (perf/graph-view-lag @ 3a09ba73) already has the lean, the edge batch and the edge-hiding fix. The view now serves before.html (the checkout), before-released-main.html (the released main) and after.html (v12), and the numbers quoted to the user are the ones against the checkout
evidence: 5 interleaved rounds: node drag x0.96 (jank 20 -> 16), pan x1.21 (jank 38 -> 19), zoom x1.07 (jank 40 -> 29); against the released main x2.26 / x2.26 / x5.42

decision: The dashed (INFERRED confidence) edges stay with vis, but not because of fidelity
why: Measured: putting them back into the batch leaves the at-rest parity unchanged (9.81% vs 9.83%) and the gestures unchanged (x1.01 / x0.98 / x0.90), so the 393 extra strokes per frame cost nothing measurable and the exclusion buys no fidelity. It is kept for the simpler reason that the confidence texture is then exactly vis own
